hypotheses.reasoning: Origin is a long-running open transaction in notif-db. At ~14:48:57 notif-db warns that TRANSACTION 99588 has been ACTIVE 97s (started ~14:47:20) while template-svc-reconciler holds a row lock on notifications, with only 1 undo entry, i.e. it is idle and not committing. From 14:49:49 template-svc UPDATE notifications statements are canceled by the 10s statement timeout because they wait on that lock (#111). notif-db then logs lock wait timeouts (#115, #117). notification-svc render calls to template-svc time out after 15s (#112). Those calls saturate notification-svc's template-svc connection pool (#134, #139), and api-gateway returns 504s (#131, #140, #153, #169). The pool saturation and 504s are downstream symptoms. Before 14:47 the system was healthy (renders 24-90ms, normal GC, no lock warnings). Redis and the worker show no errors, and the DB buffer pool hit rate is normal, so resource exhaustion is unlikely.

Connection pool exhaustion in notification-svc and gateway 504s amplify the lock stall. The trigger is the DB lock, so this is secondary. Listed only as a lower-ranked reading of the same impact lines.

verdict.recommendedAction: Identify and kill the stuck template-svc-reconciler transaction (ID 99588) in notif-db and confirm the lock is released. Fix the reconciler so it commits or rolls back promptly, and add idle-in-transaction timeouts. Add a circuit breaker or shorter timeout on template-svc /render so notification-svc pool exhaustion does not cascade to the gateway. The 504s should stop once the lock clears.
